title: wtctl shared definitions
description: Definitions referenced by every other wtctl schema (config.json embeds copies).

repo_id.description: Lowercase host, optional :port for a non-default port, then '/' and one or more path segments of [A-Za-z0-9._-], none equal to '.' or '..' (architecture section 16).

host.description: A repo id's host part: lowercase host, optional :port.

name.description: A worktree's display name and last path component.

labels.description: Sorted, unique key=value pairs; at most 32 (as termctl and claude-session).

holder.description: A holder (create, adopt, remove and forget --holder): the label value grammar, at most 64 characters.

duration.description: DURATION: a positive integer and a unit (s, m, h, d, w).

decision_ids.description: The --decision-id values, followed by the decision ids returned by pre-hooks (at most 32; invalid or excess hook-returned ids are dropped with a warning).

dev_ino.description: A recorded anchor identity: the directory's (st_dev, st_ino) as <dev>:<ino> (interface: Mount points).

branch.description: A branch name (short form, without refs/heads/).

state.description: Live: creating, active, unlinked, missing, clone_missing, partial. Tombstones: gone, removed, forgotten.

forceable_check.description: A check a human --force can override: held, the dirty and unpushed checks, and the pre-removal fetch (fetch_failed or auth_required).

command.description: Untrusted: the process's command name, chosen by whoever started it.

path.description: Untrusted: the matching cwd or open file inside the directory, as the process's /proc link or lsof reports it; non-printable bytes are escaped as \xNN; agents choose such names.

baseline_class.description: git: repository config, hooks, alternates, modules, excludes, the record's own admin entry. claude: .claude/ (except .claude/.cc-writes/), .mcp.json and CLAUDE*.md at any depth in the worktree.

sha256.description: file: content hash; directory: hash of the recursive listing of names, types and content hashes; symlink: hash of the target string; config: hash of the key's values in order.

baseline_entry.description: One side of a baseline item: absent, or its type and hash. Contents are never reported.

anchor.description: common_dir: the clone's common dir (common_id, also in the clone's row); worktree_dir: the worktree directory (dir_id); worktree_root: an owned worktree's root (base_dir, its identity in the anchors table); hooks_path: a core.hooksPath directory outside the common dir (the identity stored in its baseline item).

changed.description: true when current differs from recorded.

fs_type.description: Untrusted: the current file-system type (Linux: the mountinfo type of the opened fd's mount, e.g. ext4 or fuse.sshfs; macOS: statfs f_fstypename); a FUSE type is refused.

mount_source.description: Untrusted: the mount source (Linux: mountinfo; macOS: f_mntfromname); a FUSE file system's owner chooses it.

mount_point.description: Where the file system holding the anchor is mounted (Linux: mountinfo; macOS: f_mntonname).

anchor_change.description: An anchor with its recorded and current identity and where it is currently mounted, shown by baseline accept, by a human clone re-accepting a changed clone identity, and in create_failed anchor_changed details, so a human can tell a reboot from a mount an agent made (interface: Mount points, baseline accept).

path.description: Untrusted: a path inside the clone's git dir or the worktree; agents can create such paths.

key.description: Untrusted: a config key (section[.subsection].key) read from a file agents can write; null for items that are not config values.

detail.description: Present when the item could not be read in full, which fails safe: it always counts as changed. incomplete: a git-class directory listing exceeded remove.nested_scan_limit entries, or a file or the computation exceeded the baseline bounds (64 MiB per file; 256 MiB and remove.nested_scan_limit entries per baseline computation), or a walk reached its deadline (60 s; 300 s for one remove); mount_point: the anchor (the common dir, or a core.hooksPath directory outside it) lacks its recorded identity, or the directory, a directory on its no-follow chain from the anchor, a directory inside it or a file read for it is on another device or (Linux) mount than the anchor (in the claude-class walk: a directory or file on another mount than the worktree). after then holds the hash of the listing as far as it was read (empty for a mount point).

changed_classes.description: The classes with at least one changed item.

argv.description: The configured argv (for sh: true, the single shell string).

exit.description: Exit status; null when the step was killed (timeout) or did not exit normally.

output_tail.description: Untrusted: the last 4096 bytes of the step's combined output, mask_env values masked; project code wrote it.

state.description: none: bootstrap never ran (no steps, --no-bootstrap, adopted). interrupted: a create reclaimed by reconcile after its creator died (adopted_after_crash); bootstrap may have run partly and nothing was recorded as bootstrap-created.

steps.description: The steps of the last run, in order, up to and including the first failing step.

state.description: none: bootstrap never ran (no steps, --no-bootstrap, adopted). interrupted: a create reclaimed by reconcile after its creator died (adopted_after_crash); bootstrap may have run partly and nothing was recorded as bootstrap-created.

steps.description: The steps of the last run, in order, up to and including the first failing step.

items.description: Untrusted: a tracked path bootstrap changed; project code chose it.

tracked_changes.description: Tracked files changed by bootstrap: reported, not recorded; they count as dirty at removal.

bootstrap_result.description: The bootstrap object of the record, plus the tracked files this run changed.

step.description: path: record path vs recorded path; root: under the recorded root with no symlink below it, or the adopted path; dotgit: <path>/.git names exactly the recorded admin_dir; admin_gitdir: the admin entry's gitdir file; commondir: the admin entry's commondir; git_common_dir: git rev-parse --git-common-dir.

actual.description: Untrusted: read from files an agent in the worktree can write; null when absent or unreadable.

details.description: What failed; empty unless status is fail.

lock_reason.description: Untrusted: the content of the admin entry's locked file, which agents can write.

details.description: What failed; empty unless status is fail.

locked.description: The worktree's admin entry has a locked file (refusal locked; checked right after integrity, never overridden).

details.description: What failed (or, for warn, what was found); empty unless status is fail or warn.

baseline.description: Repo-config baseline; details are the changed items. fail: a git-class item changed (refusal repo_config_changed). warn: only claude-class items changed (remove proceeds).

details.description: What failed; empty unless status is fail.

in_use.description: In-use detection (refusal in_use). unavailable: no scanner (no /proc and no lsof); the check was skipped with a warning.

details.description: What failed; empty unless status is fail.

held.description: Holders other than the one passed with --holder (refusal held; a human --force overrides it). Worktrees only.

code.description: auth_required: the remote asked for credentials; fetch_failed: anything else.

cause.description: timeout: network_timeout expired; prune_incomplete: git exited 0 but printed an error: line (a --prune that left a stale ref); null otherwise.

message.description: Untrusted: git's stderr, from the remote.

details.description: What failed; empty unless status is fail.

fetch.description: The refresh of the clone's mirror (interface: Mirror), whose refs/heads are the tips for reachability. fail without --force exits 12 (fetch_failed or auth_required); with a human --force it is a warning and nothing counts as pushed. status reports it and skips the unpushed checks; status reports it skipped (with a warning) when the per-clone lease stayed held for 5 seconds.

path.description: Untrusted: a path inside the worktree, relative to its root; agents choose such names.

detail.description: changed: a staged, unstaged or conflicted change reported by git status; hidden_changes: the index entry has the assume-unchanged or skip-worktree bit (ls-files -v tag lowercase, S or s), which hides edits from git status (also every path outside a sparse-checkout cone; only a human --force removes such a worktree in v1).

details.description: What failed; empty unless status is fail.

tracked.description: Tracked files with changes, or with index flags that hide changes (dirty).

path.description: Untrusted: a path inside the worktree, relative to its root; agents choose such names.

details.description: What failed; empty unless status is fail.

untracked.description: Untracked, non-ignored files that are not bootstrap-created with unchanged content (dirty).

path.description: Untrusted: a path inside the worktree, relative to its root; agents choose such names.

details.description: What failed; empty unless status is fail.

ignored.description: Ignored paths neither bootstrap-created nor disposable (dirty).

detail.description: nested_repo: a .git found at path (not a recorded bootstrap_nested entry); submodule: the .git file of an initialized submodule (listed in .gitmodules at HEAD, pointing under <admin_dir>/modules/ or <common>/modules/; v1 has no recursive check, so only a human --force removes it); mount_point: a mount point below the worktree root (a directory on another device or, on Linux, another mount), which no walk crosses; incomplete: the walk exceeded remove.nested_scan_limit (path null).

path.description: Untrusted: a path inside the worktree, relative to its root; agents choose such names.

details.description: What failed; empty unless status is fail.

nested_repos.description: Nested .git files or directories anywhere below the worktree root (dirty).

details.description: What failed; empty unless status is fail.

stash.description: Stash entries made in this worktree (dirty).

detail.description: not_reachable: the commit is missing from the mirror or is not an ancestor of any mirror refs/heads tip; ancestry_unverified: the content-verified ancestry check failed (interface: Reachability); head_moved: HEAD changed after the confirmation (remove step 9; sha is the new HEAD).

details.description: What failed; empty unless status is fail.

unpushed_head.description: HEAD not pushed (interface: Reachability) and not --merged-head (unpushed).

branch.description: Untrusted: a branch name created in the worktree; null for reflog_unavailable.

sha.description: The branch tip; null for reflog_unavailable.

detail.description: reflog_unavailable: the worktree's HEAD reflog is missing or unreadable, or neither anchor is usable (no entry at or before the recorded start time and no start entry; branch and sha null).

details.description: What failed; empty unless status is fail.

unpushed_branches.description: Side branches committed in this worktree and not pushed (unpushed).

checks.description: Check results by name. Only checks that ran are present: remove stops at the first of integrity, locked, baseline, in_use and held that fails (held only without a human --force, which overrides it); status runs every check it can and reports skipped ones; a content-check refusal reports every content check. A throwaway has only in_use.

owned.description: worktree: true if created by wtctl, false if adopted. throwaway: null.

clone_path.description: The local clone. Throwaway: the clone used as source, or null.

common_dir.description: The clone's git common dir. Throwaway: null.

admin_dir.description: The worktree's admin entry <common>/worktrees/<n> (from git rev-parse --git-dir at create or adopt). null for a main worktree, a throwaway, and a worktree still creating.

common_id.description: The clone's common dir identity (st_dev, st_ino), the recorded common-dir anchor (interface: Anchor identity, Mount points); copied from the clone's row at create or adopt, changed only by a human baseline accept (wtctl never re-records it by itself). Throwaway: null.

dir_id.description: The worktree or throwaway directory's (st_dev, st_ino), recorded at create (a throwaway's after its mkdir), adopt or a reclaim after a crash; checked before wtctl deletes the directory or rewrites its pointers. null only while creating, and in a gone or forgotten tombstone of a record that never left creating.

base_dir.description: The resolved realpath root the record's path lives under (not the root config key). Owned worktree: its worktree root at create. Throwaway: the throwaway root. Adopted: null.

root_id.description: Throwaway: the throwaway root's identity (st_dev, st_ino), recorded at create (equal to that of every live throwaway under the same root). Worktree: null.

branch.description: The branch at create (or adopt), not the current one; null when detached and for throwaways. For an adopted worktree the name comes from the clone and is untrusted.

created_branch.description: wtctl created the local branch (also for a remote-only branch). Throwaway: null.

base.description: The resolved base ref the new branch was created from: refs/heads/<b>, the remote's branch (read from the mirror) when the remote has it, else the clone's local branch; null if none was used.

base_sha.description: The base's tip when the branch was created; null if no base was used.

head_at_create.description: HEAD when the worktree was created or adopted. Throwaway, or a worktree still creating: null.

ref.description: Throwaway: the checked-out commit. Worktree: --ref, else null.

source.description: Throwaway: the source used; while creating, the requested --source (auto possible). Worktree: null.

depth.description: Throwaway: history depth, 0 = full history. While creating, the requested depth; once active, the depth used (a local source copies the full history, 0, unless --depth 1). Worktree: null.

fetch_url.description: Worktree: the clone fetch URL recorded at create or adopt (interface: Clone resolution), without userinfo. Throwaway: the URL fetched from, or the clone's path for a local source; null while creating, until the source is chosen.

remote.description: The clone's remote whose URL was recorded. Throwaway: null.

holders.description: Sorted holders added by create --holder and adopt --holder (owned and adopted worktrees); remove refuses held while another holder remains. Empty for throwaways.

baseline_digest.description: Throwaway, or a worktree whose baseline is not recorded yet (creating): null.

missing_since.description: When reconcile first saw the directory missing; null otherwise.

removed_at.description: When the record became a tombstone; null while live.

last_error.description: Untrusted: the last failure's message, which may quote git or the file system.

record.description: A wtctl record (interface: Record object). Fields that do not apply are null.

to.description: null when the tombstone was deleted.

action.description: What reconcile did (e.g. repair, admin_entry_delete, tombstone_delete).

branch.description: Untrusted: a branch name from the clone.

message.description: Untrusted: git's stderr, a pointer-rewrite failure message, or, for kept_unpushed, the condition that kept the admin entry.

kind_of.description: stray: throwaway (a directory under the throwaway root with no live record), clone_tmp (a leftover *.wtctl-tmp-* clone directory) or mirror (a mirror no clone in state.db names). Other kinds: null or omitted.

admin_entry.description: gone: absent (the clone's admin entry was already gone; nothing was deleted). Other kinds: null or omitted.

report.description: A reconcile report. gone: id, path, admin_entry: absent, and branch when a created branch was kept (an owned missing record whose admin entry was already gone, marked gone after the grace period with nothing to delete); gone_with_unpushed: id, branch, tip (the record is gone, its unpushed branch kept); kept_unpushed: id, tip, message (an admin entry kept because its HEAD is neither reachable from a local branch nor pushed, it holds submodule git dirs or per-worktree refs, or its HEAD reflog names an unpushed commit since the recorded start; tip is the entry's HEAD or that commit); adopted_gone: id, path (an adopted record marked gone after the grace period); adopted_after_crash: id, path (a creating worktree whose creator died, found intact and made active); abandoned: id, path, and branch when a created branch was kept (a creating record whose creator died and that could not be reclaimed: gone if its path was absent, else left creating for a human forget, or skipped because a process is in its planned path; the changes list shows which); stray: path, kind_of (a throwaway directory with no live record, a leftover *.wtctl-tmp-* clone directory, or an orphaned mirror; never deleted); unlinked: id, path; clone_missing: id, clone_path; moved_clone: id, clone_path (the record is clone_missing; a re-resolved clone at clone_path names the record's path; reconcile changes nothing else, and a human re-attaches the record with baseline accept); fetch_failed: clone_path, message.

post_hook_entry.description: async: true runs the hook detached (post-hooks only).

dir.description: An absolute directory, or one starting with ~/ (expanded once).

sh.description: true: argv[0] runs through sh -c, and argv must have one element.

clone_url.description: Overrides the host's template; may be a file:// URL or a path.

copy_env.description: Env-file globs relative to the main worktree.

pass_env.description: hosts.*.token_env variables passed to steps after all (they are stripped by default).

disposable.description: Replaces the global list; null: the global list.

allow_filters.description: Replaces the global list; null: the global list.

token_env.description: Env var holding an HTTPS token; used when set and non-empty.

token_command.description: argv (no shell; an argument equal to {host} is replaced) whose stdout is the token; used when token_env gives none. 10-second timeout.
